principles: Reuse the shipped freshness machinery (materialHash / storyFilesHash + demote-on-drift), never a parallel drift model.
Mechanical determinism over semantic cleverness: normalization and drift are byte-level and reproducible; human semantic judgment lives only in Phase-2 re-attestation.
Stay advisory in Phase 1: never block a gate, because a block without a recovery path wedges stories.
Minimize false positives by binding to the narrowest material that still covers the claim; a false-positive-noisy advisory trains operators to ignore it.
Grandfather, do not break: userSees with no snapshot are legacy-unbound and reported, never errored.
drivers: F-027/F-060/F-059: frozen claims silently outlived the code they asserted about -- the failure this story detects.
Operator false-positive tolerance is low (memory fa1777b: an advisory operators learn to ignore has no effect); the material binding must resist unrelated churn.
package.json / main-merge drift is the dominant unrelated-drift source (memory e5bcf07); binding to whole-tree material would fire on every sibling merge.

options.name: A: whole-tree materialHash
pros: Catches every code change under a frozen claim
cons: Extreme false positives: any unrelated file change or main-merge stales every userSees
Trains operators to ignore the advisory, poisoning Phase 2's eventual gate

options.name: B: storyFilesHash (story-diff-scoped)
pros: Covers exactly the files this story delivers -- the claim's actual support
Excludes unrelated main-merge churn by construction (B-5a9a), addressing the top false-positive source
Reuses the B-5a9a/B-d243/B-edf1 machinery this story already extends
A userSees asserts THIS story's delivery, so its supporting code is in the story diff
cons: Will not flag drift in a file the claim depends on that is outside the story diff (rare; the claim is delivered by the story's own diff)
storyFilesHash includes package.json when the story wires npm scripts, so a DONE auto-bump can move it -- expected and asserted in the smoke

options.name: C: per-CHK-item file set
pros: Most precise: binds each userSees to only the files that delivered it
cons: Requires per-item file provenance (from plan.md Files or the delivering commit) that does not exist today
Over-engineered for a non-blocking detect-only Phase 1 (YAGNI)
More surface for its own bugs before the value is validated

rationale: storyFilesHash covers exactly the files this story delivers (the claim's support) and by construction excludes unrelated main-merge churn -- the dominant false-positive source (memory e5bcf07) -- so it satisfies drivers 2 and 3 while reusing the B-5a9a/B-d243/B-edf1 machinery instead of a parallel model (principle 1). Option C is more precise but its per-item provenance is unjustified for a non-blocking detect-only milestone (principle 4 / YAGNI); option A is the false-positive swamp that gets the advisory ignored. The normalized claim-digest remains a co-equal secondary trigger, so an edited userSees is caught regardless of the material choice (bidirectional binding). The known package.json / DONE-bump interaction is acknowledged: the smoke asserts an unrelated in-tree change produces NO drift and a story-owned change DOES, and the false-positive rate is to be measured on real stories before Phase 2 hardens this into a gate.

preMortem.scenario: The advisory fires on nearly every story (high false-positive noise), operators learn to ignore it, and Phase 2's eventual gate inherits a distrusted signal.
preMortem.trigger: Material bound to whole-tree materialHash, or a binding that counts unrelated main-merge / package.json churn as drift.
preMortem.consequence: The feature becomes worse than nothing -- it normalizes ignoring evidence-integrity advisories.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind to storyFilesHash (option B). The smoke asserts an unrelated in-tree change AND a whitespace-only claim edit both produce NO drift; the false-positive rate is measured on a sample of real stories before Phase 2 hardens it into a gate.

preMortem.trigger: The drift check is wired into an existing gate's pass/fail (review guard, delivery-check, or DONE) instead of a standalone read-only path.
preMortem.consequence: Every story with a drifted or legacy-unbound userSees wedges with no recovery command until Phase 2 ships.
preMortem.mitigation: Expose only a read-only command plus an optional story_get field; the smoke asserts the advisory never changes any gate verdict; no edit to canPassReview / delivery / DONE gate logic in this story.

preMortem.scenario: The snapshot is captured at the wrong moment, so drift is never detected or is always detected.
preMortem.trigger: The attestation hook fires before the userSees is actually delivered (snapshots pre-delivery material) or re-snapshots on every read (never goes stale).
preMortem.consequence: False negatives (real drift missed) or a self-healing snapshot that silently defeats the purpose.
preMortem.mitigation: Capture the snapshot once, at a well-defined delivery point (checklist_update status=done), immutable thereafter (mirror the B-ec67 pin-once model). The smoke drives status=done, then mutates material and asserts drift, and asserts that re-running the check does NOT re-snapshot.

preMortem.scenario: Someone edits userSees after delivery to match the new behavior and the old attestation silently keeps passing.
preMortem.trigger: Claim-digest omitted from the drift signal (material-only binding).
preMortem.consequence: A frozen-field promise is quietly rewritten with no re-attestation -- the exact F-027 class this story exists to close.
preMortem.mitigation: Bidirectional binding: the normalized claim-digest is a co-equal trigger; editing userSees changes the digest -> drift -> re_attestation. The smoke asserts a non-whitespace claim-text edit is detected.
